questions.question: When a fuel burns in air, what is the primary way energy is transferred?
options: By heating the surroundings
By absorbing heat from the surroundings
By cooling the immediate environment
By destroying matter

questions.question: How can we experimentally compare the amounts of energy transferred by burning different fuels in a school laboratory?
options: By measuring the volume of gas produced in a syringe
By heating water in a boiling tube and measuring its temperature rise
By measuring the mass of the fuel before it is made
By looking at the color of the fuel's flame

questions.question: To make a fair comparison between the energy released by different fuels, which variable must be kept constant regarding the fuels themselves?
options: The volume of oxygen they consume
The mass of fuel used for each measurement
The colour of the fuel container
The shape of the match used to light them

questions.question: When investigating the energy output of different fuels by heating water, what must be kept the same for the water at the start of each test?
options: Only the density of the water
Only the container material
Both the initial temperature and the volume of the water
Both the boiling point and the mass of the container

questions.question: When looking at a cooling curve graph of a substance, how do we identify where a state change is occurring?
options: By a steep, sudden drop in temperature
By a flat horizontal section (plateau)
By a vertical line going straight down
By a steady, constant increase in temperature

questions.question: What happens to energy and state when a hot substance cools down?
options: It absorbs energy from the surroundings and may melt or boil
It transfers energy to the surroundings by heating and it may condense or freeze
It destroys energy and remains in the same state permanently
It transfers energy to the surroundings and always turns into a gas

questions.question: If a chemical reaction is described as exothermic, what temperature change would you observe in its surroundings?
options: The temperature remains exactly the same
The temperature decreases
The temperature increases
The temperature fluctuates randomly

questions.question: When an endothermic chemical reaction takes place in a beaker, what happens to the temperature of the surroundings?
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays completely constant
It rises to boiling point immediately

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the transfer of energy in an exothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings
Energy is created from nothing within the products
No energy transfer occurs during the reaction

questions.question: From where to where is energy transferred during an endothermic chemical reaction?
options: From the products to the surroundings
From the reactants to the atmosphere only
From the surroundings to the products
Energy is transferred out of the system into space

questions.question: Which group of state changes are all endothermic processes?
options: Melting, evaporation, and boiling
Condensing, freezing, and melting
Freezing, condensing, and boiling
Evaporation, condensing, and freezing

questions.question: Why are condensing and freezing classified as exothermic processes?
options: They absorb energy from the surroundings
They release energy to the surroundings
They do not involve any change in energy
They require continuous heating to occur

questions.question: Which sources are responsible for generating over half of the electricity in the UK?
options: Coal, nuclear power, and biomass
Natural gas, oil, and coal
The Sun, wind, and falling water
Geothermal energy and waves only

questions.question: Which fossil fuel is no longer used to generate electricity in UK power stations?
options: Natural gas
Coal
Crude oil
Wood

questions.question: Which of the following groups of fuels all produce greenhouse gases and pollutants when burned?
options: Wind, solar, and falling water
Natural gas, oil, waste, and wood
Hydrogen, wind, and tidal energy
Solar energy, geothermal, and nuclear

questions.question: Why will renewable energy resources not run out?
options: Because they are stored in infinite quantities deep inside the Earth
Because they are replenished more quickly than we use them up
Because we have stopped using electricity altogether
Because they do not require any physical processes to generate power

questions.question: How do solar panels differ from wind turbines and steam power stations in how they generate electricity?
options: They require steam to turn their internal gears
They produce electricity without electric generators
They must burn wood to function
They rely on spinning coils of wire inside them
